spec.name: Earnings drift v11
spec.notes: Earnings surprise screen, slow rebalance. Adds the vendor's revised sentiment score.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.8, annual return 5%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.81 to 1.13 (change -0.69).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.81 to 1.22. Changed by strict mode: fields sentiment_revised.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.77 (as submitted, 8 bps: 1.81); it breaks even at 86.4 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.81 against 1.81 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 0.14 against 1.81 in research, a gap of +1.67.
The best year gives 23% of total P&L (year 6) and calm regimes give 74%; Sharpe is 1.78 in calm and 2.1 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.03, so the claimed 1.80 becomes 1.77 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.02 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.02, 95th percentile 0.49).
Perturbing the 1 numeric value in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.81 to as low as 1.52 (as low as 1.62 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (23 days) give 35% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 21% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
